narrative: The model estimates a 79% probability that you will leave your job. That does not mean it knows your intentions, but it places you in a high-risk group, so the organization sees a promotion as an investment you may not stay long enough to justify; this is why you are denied a promotion at this time. The strongest signal was that you have received other job opportunities while in this role—only about a quarter of employees predicted to stay report this—so it pushes strongly toward leaving. The second strongest was your overall experience of six to ten years, also toward leaving; most employees predicted to stay have only one to five years overall, so your broader experience makes you look more mobile. The third was your one-to-five years in the current organization, again toward leaving, though this is common among stayers and therefore a more modest factor. Next, the organization should discuss your career path and promotion criteria openly, ask what would keep you, and address retention concerns such as development, recognition, and workload balance. You should clarify whether you intend to stay and what support or role change would make that worthwhile.
